contentSections.heading: The seat that's right for your six-month-old is the wrong one entirely for your five-year-old.

paragraphs.text: NSW road rules are specific about this for good reason: a rear-facing capsule for infants, a forward-facing harnessed seat once they're steadier, then a booster as they grow into adult belts properly. Getting it wrong isn't just a paperwork issue, it's the difference between a restraint that actually does its job and one that doesn't.

We'd rather ask two quick questions when you book, your child's age and roughly their size, than turn up with whatever seat happened to be in the boot. If you're travelling with your own seat and just need the car, that's fine too, just mention it.

contentSections.heading: Not a hypothetical persona list, these are the bookings that actually come through.

bulletList.text: A newborn's first flight: Nervous parents, a capsule that needs to be exactly right, and a driver who isn't in a rush while everyone gets settled.
Grandparents flying in to meet the baby: Booked by the new parents, picked up solo, with a capsule ready even though they didn't have to think about it.
A family of five coming home from holiday: Three kids, three different seat types, one pram, and a flight that landed later than planned.
Interstate or overseas visitors with young kids: No car seat of their own to bring, and no interest in buying one for a week-long trip.
A family flying home after a hospital stay: A newborn, sometimes still quite small, and parents who'd rather not be figuring out a capsule for the first time that day.
A family reunion or wedding weekend: Multiple children across different ages arriving together, each needing a different seat, sorted in one booking.

faq.question: Do I need to bring my own baby seat?
faq.answer: No. Tell us your child's age and roughly their size when you book, and we'll have the right capsule, seat or booster fitted before we arrive. If you'd rather use your own seat, that's fine too, just let us know.

faq.question: How do you know which seat my child actually needs?
faq.answer: Age is the starting point, roughly a rear-facing capsule under six months, a forward-facing harnessed seat from six months to around four years, then a booster from about four to seven. Size matters too.

faq.question: Is the seat actually fitted properly, or just placed in the car?
faq.answer: Fitted properly. Our drivers install capsules, seats and boosters correctly before your child gets in, it's not adjusted on the go once you're already moving.

faq.question: I've got three kids of different ages, can you handle that in one booking?
faq.answer: Yes. Tell us each child's age when you book and we'll bring a vehicle fitted with the right seat for every one of them.

faq.question: Will the price change once I'm in the car?
faq.answer: No. The fare you're quoted is the fare you pay, with any applicable WSI airport charges confirmed in your quote. No meter, no surge pricing, no surprises at drop-off.

faq.question: How much notice do you actually need?
faq.answer: A few hours' notice lets us confirm we've got the right seat size on hand. Shorter notice is worth a call anyway, we'll do what we can.

faq.question: What if our flight lands early or gets delayed?
faq.answer: Your flight number is linked to the booking, so your driver's arrival shifts with it automatically. No need to call us.

faq.question: Do you run family flights that leave really early or really late?
faq.answer: Yes. Western Sydney Airport is designed to operate without a curfew, so once it opens, 4am and midnight family flights are expected to be part of the normal schedule there - and we'll be ready to cover them from opening day.

faq.question: How is TipTop different from a Western Sydney Airport shuttle service?
faq.answer: TipTop provides a private, door-to-door vehicle matched to your passenger and luggage numbers, with no shared stops or interchanges. Vehicle size, wheelchair accessibility and child seats can all be arranged in advance, with a confirmed quotation including known charges before you travel.
